newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish prisoners step up hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Turkish prisoners step up hunger strike.

text.p: More than 75 prisoners in two high-security prisons in Turkey's southeastern Erzurum province began an indefinite hunger strike to protest against prison conditions, Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.

Anatolian said the prisoners were demanding the government fulfill commitments made in July after 12 leftist inmates starved themselves to death in western Turkey to demand an end to mistreatment and better access to family and lawyers.

Another 80 inmates have erected barricades inside a prison in the western province of Canakkale, and an inmate in eastern Batman province was in serious condition after setting himself alight in protest.
Pro-Kurdish activists said members of the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), who five days ago began a limited hunger strike at Canakkale, have decided to continue the strike indefinitely.
They were protesting at the death of fellow PKK members during a riot in high-security Diyarbakir prison, which has prompted an investigation by the Justice Ministry.
Three inmates set themselves alight in an Istanbul prison at the weekend in protest at the deaths in Diyarbakir and two of them sustained serious injuries.
